question: In Goldfinger, Bond's Aston Martin hides a red button inside the top of the gear stick. Press it and an unwanted passenger is gone. What does the button fire?
source_excerpt: The gear lever hid a small red button. Pressing it released a section of the roof and fired the passenger ejector seat.

extra.why_interesting: Nearly everyone has a mental picture of the gadget-packed Bond car. The question lets them pull out the most outrageous gadget, and the gear-stick button detail makes the answer feel like a reward.
extra.verification_notes: In Goldfinger the DB5's gear-knob red button fires the passenger ejector seat; no newer development changes this (https://www.thejamesbonddossier.com/lifestyle/cars/the-gadgets-of-the-db5.htm).

explanation: The ejector seat flings the passenger out through a panel in the roof. It became the most famous single gadget in Bond history, and toy versions of the car sold in the millions.

question: Tourist boats head for a needle-shaped limestone rock rising out of the sea, which everyone now calls 'James Bond Island' because a villain's lair was filmed there. Which country is it in?
source_excerpt: Khao Phing Kan is an island in Thailand, in Phang Nga Bay northeast of Phuket. The islands are commonly known in English as James Bond Island.

extra.why_interesting: Players don't expect a film location to have literally renamed a place on tourist maps. The limestone-pillar and boat-trip footholds let them reason their way to Southeast Asia.
extra.verification_notes: Ko Tapu / Khao Phing Kan ('James Bond Island') in Phang Nga Bay is in Thailand, featured as Scaramanga's lair in The Man with the Golden Gun (https://Www.wikipedia.org/wiki/Ko_Tapu).

explanation: It is Khao Phing Kan in Phang Nga Bay, the hideout of Scaramanga in The Man with the Golden Gun. The film's nickname stuck so well that it has largely replaced the real name with visitors.

question: The white Lotus that turns into a submarine in The Spy Who Loved Me was sold at auction in 2013 for nearly a million dollars. The buyer, a famous tech entrepreneur, said he wanted to make it transform for real. Who bought it?
source_excerpt: "I was disappointed to learn that it can't actually transform. What I'm going to do is upgrade it with a Tesla electric powertrain and try to make it transform for real."

extra.why_interesting: A movie prop ending up with a modern tech mogul is an unexpected link between 1970s Bond and today. The 'make it really transform' detail is a fair foothold toward someone known for futuristic vehicles.
extra.verification_notes: Multiple outlets confirm Elon Musk bought the Lotus Esprit submarine at the 2013 RM Auctions sale for roughly $866K–$997K and said he wanted to make it work as a real submarine; no newer event changes the buyer.

explanation: Musk bought the original underwater prop, which had sat forgotten in a storage unit for years until someone bought it blind for about 100 dollars. He said he was disappointed to learn that it couldn't actually transform, and planned to fit it with a Tesla electric drive.

question: Which of these James Bond actors starred in only a single official Bond film?
source_excerpt: He played James Bond in On Her Majesty's Secret Service (1969)

extra.why_interesting: All four are genuine Bond actors, so nothing on the surface gives it away. Players have to recall that one of them walked away after a single outing, and many will be tempted by Dalton, who also had a short run.
extra.verification_notes: Lazenby is the only one of the four with a single Eon Bond film (On Her Majesty's Secret Service, 1969); Dalton has 2, Brosnan 4, Craig 5; see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/George_Lazenby.

explanation: Lazenby was an Australian model with almost no acting experience. He turned down a multi-film contract after On Her Majesty's Secret Service, while Dalton made two films, Brosnan four and Craig five.

question: Classic vampires burn up in sunlight. In Twilight, what happens instead to Robert Pattinson's Edward Cullen when he steps into the sun?
source_excerpt: Edward's skin sparkles in the sunlight.

extra.why_interesting: Everyone knows sunlight destroys vampires, so the player starts from 'he burns'. The Twilight twist, much mocked and endlessly memed, is that he simply glitters.
extra.verification_notes: Edward's skin sparkles like diamonds in direct sunlight in Twilight, as the Prime Focus VFX 'Diamond Skin' effect page describes; no newer event contradicts this.

explanation: Twilight vampires glitter like diamonds in daylight, so the Cullens avoid the sun to keep their secret rather than to stay alive. Pattinson later joked about how hard it was to take the sparkle scene seriously.

question: Edward Cullen looks seventeen, but in the Twilight story he was born in Chicago at the start of the 1900s. Which real deadly pandemic was killing him when he was turned into a vampire?
source_excerpt: Carlisle Cullen transformed him into a vampire in 1918 to prevent him from dying in the Spanish influenza epidemic.

extra.why_interesting: Players see Edward as a moody teenager and don't think of him as a man born over a century ago. Learning that he was saved from a real historical pandemic changes how they picture him.
extra.verification_notes: Wikipedia confirms Edward was born in 1901 and turned in 1918 in Chicago while dying of the Spanish influenza epidemic.

explanation: Carlisle Cullen found Edward dying of the Spanish flu in 1918 and turned him to save his life. That makes Pattinson's 'teenage' heartthrob more than a hundred years old.

question: Robert Pattinson's Batman is a gloomy, sleepless loner, and the film sets that mood with a slow, haunting song by a famous Seattle grunge band. Which band?
source_excerpt: It serves as a background for Bruce Wayne's monologues in the movie.

extra.why_interesting: Superhero films usually rely on big orchestral scores. Here a brooding grunge track sets the mood, and many players will remember it once 'grunge' points them toward the obvious band.
extra.verification_notes: Nirvana's 'Something in the Way' is featured in The Batman (2022) per https://slashfilm.com/784457/the-nirvana-song-in-the-batman-explained; no newer development contradicts this.

explanation: The song is 'Something in the Way' from Nirvana's album Nevermind. Director Matt Reeves said he pictured Bruce Wayne as a reclusive Kurt Cobain-style rock star, and the song's streams surged after the trailer came out.

question: In the sci-fi film Mickey 17, Robert Pattinson plays a space colonist whose job is to take on missions that will kill him. So what does the 17 in the title stand for?
source_excerpt: seventeenth, later eighteenth, iteration

extra.why_interesting: Players assume the number is an age, a year or a sequel count. The real reason is darkly comic: he has already died sixteen times. The stem says his job is to die, so a player can reason their way there.
extra.verification_notes: Wikipedia confirms Mickey 17 is the seventeenth iteration/clone in the reprinting sequence; 'clone' vs 'iteration' is only a minor wording quibble.

explanation: Every time Mickey dies, the crew simply prints a fresh body with his memories. The trouble starts when number 17 survives, and number 18 gets printed anyway.

question: Before making the very first Grand Theft Auto, the same small Scottish studio had a huge hit with a cute puzzle game. In it, you stop tiny green-haired creatures from marching off cliffs. What was that game called?
source_excerpt: Lemmings was released in February 1991, about six years before the first Grand Theft Auto in 1997.

extra.why_interesting: People assume America's most notorious crime-sim began somewhere like Los Angeles. It actually came from a small Scottish studio best known for a cute, harmless puzzle game. The description gives older players a real path to the answer.
extra.verification_notes: DMA Design (Dundee) made Lemmings (1991) before GTA (1997), per Wikipedia.

explanation: DMA Design of Dundee made Lemmings in 1991 and then the original GTA. The studio is now Rockstar North, still based in Scotland.

question: True or false: GTA V reached a billion dollars in sales faster than any movie in history had ever done.
source_excerpt: reached $1 billion in sales after just three days on 20 September 2013, making it also the fastest entertainment property of any kind to reach the $1 billion landmark.

extra.why_interesting: Most people assume Hollywood blockbusters are the biggest money-makers in entertainment. A video game beating every film to a billion dollars feels too big to be true, but it is.
extra.verification_notes: GTA V hit $1B in 3 days (Guinness), faster than the fastest film, Avengers: Endgame at 5 days; the newer Spider-Man: Brand New Day took 6 days, so no film has beaten it.

explanation: True. GTA V passed one billion dollars in just three days in 2013, earning a Guinness World Record as the fastest entertainment product of any kind to do it at the time.

question: Nvidia's founders planned the company over coffee in a booth at a cheap American diner chain. Jensen Huang had once washed dishes at the same chain as a teenager. Which chain was it?
source_excerpt: Denny's dishwasher

extra.why_interesting: Players picture a trillion-dollar tech giant starting in a garage or a lab, but it was planned over coffee in a cheap diner. The teen-job clue lets them reason toward a famous American diner chain.
extra.verification_notes: Nvidia was planned at a Denny's on Berryessa Road in San Jose and Huang washed dishes at Denny's as a teen, so the chain matches (Fortune).

explanation: The company was dreamed up in 1993 at a Denny's in San Jose, and that booth now carries a plaque calling it the birthplace of a trillion-dollar company.

question: The name Nvidia comes from a Latin word for one of the seven deadly sins. The company's green logo is a hint. Which sin is it?
source_excerpt: The final name comes from "invidia," the Latin word for envy.

extra.why_interesting: Most people assume the name is invented tech jargon. It is actually a Latin word for a deadly sin, and the green logo is a clue the player can use.
extra.verification_notes: Wikipedia states Nvidia's name derives from 'invidia', the Latin word for envy, which is one of the seven deadly sins.

explanation: 'Invidia' is Latin for envy, so the green logo is a nod to being 'green with envy'. The founders wanted their chips to make rivals jealous.

question: True or false: Nvidia boss Jensen Huang has the company's logo tattooed on his arm.
source_excerpt: got a tattoo of the company's logo on his left shoulder

extra.why_interesting: A CEO tattooing his own company's logo sounds like an invented anecdote, so most players will guess false. It is true.
extra.verification_notes: Huang has an Nvidia logo tattoo on his arm/shoulder, acquired after his promise tied to the $100 share price (Britannica says left shoulder, others say arm); nothing newer contradicts this.

explanation: It's true. Huang got the tattoo after Nvidia's stock first passed 100 dollars a share, and he has joked that it hurt so much he will never get another.

question: Odysseus blinds the Cyclops, who screams for help. The other Cyclopes come running, then shrug and walk away. What had Odysseus told the Cyclops his name was?
source_excerpt: Odysseus tells Polyphemus that his name is 'Nobody' (Outis)

extra.why_interesting: Players may half-remember the blinding but not that the escape turns on a pun. Once they hear it, the trick feels obvious and clever, and it works just as well in translation.
extra.verification_notes: Odysseus tells Polyphemus his name is 'Outis' (Nobody) in Odyssey Book 9, which is why the other Cyclopes leave; see https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Polyphemus

explanation: When Polyphemus shouts that 'Nobody' is hurting him, his neighbours decide nothing is wrong. One of the oldest wordplay jokes in literature saves Odysseus's life.

question: Odysseus left his young son in the care of an old friend. The goddess Athena later borrowed that friend's appearance to give the boy advice. What was the friend's name, now an everyday word?
source_excerpt: Athena takes the form of Mentor to guide Telemachus on his voyage

extra.why_interesting: Everyone uses the word at work, but few realise it is a character's name from the Odyssey, and that the 'wise mentor' was really a goddess in disguise.
extra.verification_notes: Mentor was entrusted with Telemachus, Athena took his form, and the word 'mentor' derives from him (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mentor_(Odyssey)).

explanation: The word 'mentor' comes straight from him. Fittingly, the best advice credited to him actually came from Athena, the goddess of wisdom.

question: Odysseus comes home after twenty years, disguised as a ragged beggar. One member of his household knows him at a glance, then dies on the spot. Who?
source_excerpt: Upon seeing his master return home, Argos dies.

extra.why_interesting: Players expect the wife or the son to see through the disguise first. The real answer is the most moving moment in the epic, and anyone who has owned a dog can reason their way to it.
extra.verification_notes: Argos recognizes the disguised Odysseus in Odyssey Book 17 and dies immediately; Eurycleia recognizes him later by his scar and survives, so the answer is unique (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Argos_(dog)).

explanation: Old Argos, lying neglected on a dung heap, lifts his ears and wags his tail at his master, then dies. Odysseus has to hide a tear so he won't give himself away.

question: Godzilla's famous roar wasn't made by an animal at all. The composer rubbed a leather glove along the strings of a large orchestral instrument. Which one?
source_excerpt: produced by rubbing a resin-covered leather glove along the loosened strings of a double bass.

extra.why_interesting: Everyone assumes the roar came from an animal recording or an electronic effect. It was actually a classical instrument played with a glove, and the player can work out the instrument from 'large' and 'strings'.
extra.verification_notes: Wikipedia's Akira Ifukube article confirms the roar came from a resin-covered leather glove rubbed along loosened double bass strings.

explanation: Akira Ifukube dragged a resin-coated glove down loosened double bass strings and slowed the recording. That eerie screech became the most recognisable monster sound in film.

question: A Japanese Godzilla film made for under 15 million dollars beat big Hollywood blockbusters to win an Oscar. In which category?
source_excerpt: Godzilla Minus One Is Officially The First Movie In The Franchise To Win An Oscar

extra.why_interesting: Players expect a low-budget Japanese monster film to lose to Hollywood on spectacle. It won precisely in the category where big studios spend the most money.
extra.verification_notes: Godzilla Minus One won the Best Visual Effects Oscar at the 96th Academy Awards with a reported budget of about $10-15M; no later events change this (https://slashfilm.com/1536328/godzilla-minus-one-officially-first-movie-in-franchise-to-win-oscar).

explanation: Godzilla Minus One won Best Visual Effects, the franchise's first ever Oscar, seventy years after the original film. Its budget was a small fraction of the Hollywood films it beat.

question: True or false: Godzilla has been officially registered as a resident of a Tokyo city ward.
source_excerpt: Godzilla was granted special residency in Tokyo's Shinjuku ward as a newly installed model of the lizard's head drew visitors.

extra.why_interesting: It sounds like an absurd joke claim, so most players will say false. A real city government actually issued the fictional monster official paperwork.
extra.verification_notes: Shinjuku ward granted Godzilla a special (symbolic) residency certificate in 2015, so 'True' holds in the ward's own framing, though it was a promotional gesture and not a legal registration.

explanation: Shinjuku ward granted Godzilla a special residency certificate and made it a tourism ambassador. Its giant head now peers over a hotel rooftop there.

question: The Habsburgs married their own cousins so often that one feature kept appearing in their royal portraits, generation after generation. Which part of the face was it?
source_excerpt: this is often also referred to as Habsburg chin, Habsburg's chin, Habsburg jaw or Habsburg's jaw.

extra.why_interesting: Players know royal portraits look stiff and grand. The twist is that one family's portraits keep showing the same face, a visible result of generations of cousin marriages.
extra.verification_notes: Habsburg jaw (mandibular prognathism, also called Habsburg chin or lip) is the well-documented trait; Wikipedia treats the lip and chin names as the same condition.

explanation: The 'Habsburg jaw' was a jutting lower jaw passed down through inbreeding. It was so severe in Spain's King Charles II that he reportedly struggled to chew his food.

question: In the 1950s, a teenage Austrian actress became a European sensation playing Empress Sisi in a trilogy of romantic films. She later moved to Paris and became a star of French cinema. Who was she?
source_excerpt: decided to live and to work in France

extra.why_interesting: Many players know the sugary 'Sissi' films or know Romy Schneider as a serious French film star, but they may not connect the two. The actress spent years trying to escape the role that made her famous.
extra.verification_notes: Romy Schneider, born in Vienna, starred in the 1955-57 Sissi trilogy as a teenager and later became a star of French cinema (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Romy_Schneider).

explanation: Romy Schneider came to resent the sweet Sisi image and turned down a fourth film. She did play Elisabeth once more, in Visconti's 'Ludwig', as a much darker and older empress.

question: Empress Sisi's hair reached almost to her ankles, and washing it took nearly a whole day. Her servants used raw eggs mixed with which alcoholic drink?
source_excerpt: hair washed with a mixture of egg and cognac

extra.why_interesting: An egg hair mask sounds like a modern home remedy. Hearing that an empress also poured expensive brandy on her head makes for a delightful 'really?' moment, and players can reach the answer by thinking of a luxury drink.
extra.verification_notes: Multiple sources, including the Sisi Museum, say her hair was washed with egg and cognac; no contradicting evidence found.

explanation: Her hair was washed with eggs and cognac roughly every few weeks. On those days she cancelled almost everything else, and a hairdresser reportedly had to present any fallen hairs to her.

question: True or false: Empress Sisi of Austria had a tattoo of an anchor on her shoulder.
source_excerpt: The Empress had a tattoo of an anchor on her shoulder done in 1888 to represent her undying love for the sea.

extra.why_interesting: Players picture a corseted 19th-century empress and assume a tattoo is a modern, rebellious thing. The truth is that Sisi got one in middle age.
extra.verification_notes: Multiple sources report Sisi got an anchor tattoo on her shoulder in 1888; the left/right shoulder detail varies but doesn't affect the question.

explanation: True. She had the anchor tattooed in her fifties, a sign of her love of the sea, and her husband Franz Joseph was reportedly horrified.
